https://www.theverge.com/science/1013954.headline: The fossil fuel comeback is here

spans.sentence: While the US still generates 60 percent of its electricity from fossil fuels , renewables have quickly gained ground.
Solar was the fastest-growing source of new electricity generation that year, accounting for 81 percent of added capacity.

Plans for new fossil fuel infrastructure climbed from just 5 percent of all new capacity in 2024 to 30 percent by the second quarter of 2026, according to the new report, which analyzes data from the US Energy Information Administration.
If the trend continues, fossil fuels could make up 70 percent of the development pipeline by the end of the decade.
Planned fossil capacity would reach 68 gigawatts by 2030, reflecting a 45 percent jump from construction plans just six months ago.
But for now, renewable energy projects are being canceled at a faster clip than fossil fuels, at 4.9 percent compared to 2.9 percent of projects, respectively.

New utility-scale solar and wind farms still beat gas when it comes to cost, coming in at $68 to $69 per megawatt-hour on average compared to $90 per megawatt-hour for new combined-cycle natural gas plants, the report finds.

spans.sentence: All of these laptops have the same N1X chip with 20 CPU cores and 6,144 GPU CUDA cores, and they’re all wildly expensive — ranging from the HP OmniBook at $3,199.99 to the Asus ProArt’s $6,999.99.

I mostly game on my desktop, where I’m spoiled by using an RTX 5090 on a 32-inch 4K screen every day with maxed-out game settings, but I didn’t mind the look of medium settings on a 15-inch display.

The excellent Titanfall 2 VR mod worked, and it seemed to run fine at first, but lost a little stability after a few minutes.
